question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution is related with provision for just and humane conditions of work and maternity relief?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 42**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 42 of the Indian Constitution is part of the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP).
 
• It directs the State to make provision for securing just and humane conditions of work and for maternity relief.
 
• The Directive Principles are guidelines for the framing of laws by the government and aim to create social and economic conditions under which citizens can lead a good life.
 
• Although non-justiciable, these principles are fundamental in the governance of the country and it is the duty of the State to apply these principles in making laws.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 42: Just and humane conditions of work and maternity relief**

 
 
• Article 42 falls under Part IV of the Indian Constitution, which lists the Directive Principles of State Policy.
 
• This Article emphasizes the importance of ensuring fair and decent working conditions for workers.
 
• It also underscores the significance of maternity relief, advocating for policies that support women during pregnancy and childbirth.
 
• The provision ensures the well-being of workers and promotes gender equality in the workplace.
 
 
 
• **Article 45: Provision for early childhood care and education to children below the age of six years**
 
 
• This Article directs the State to provide free and compulsory education for children until they complete the age of six years.
 
• It highlights the importance of early childhood care and education in the overall development of children.
 
 
 
• **Article 44: Uniform civil code for the citizens**
 
 
• Article 44 directs the State to endeavor to secure a uniform civil code for all citizens throughout the territory of India.
 
• The aim is to ensure that all citizens are governed by the same set of secular laws, irrespective of their religion.
 
 
 
• **Article 43: Living wage, etc., for workers**
 
 
• This Article directs the State to secure a living wage, ensuring decent standards of life and full enjoyment of leisure and social and cultural opportunities for all workers.
 
• The provision emphasizes the importance of fair remuneration and the overall well-being of workers.
